title: AI & LLM Foundations for Developers: Tokens, Cost, Hallucinations & Choosing a Model
concept: Understand how a large language model produces text at the level an engineer needs: tokens and probabilities, the context window, temperature, cost and latency, why models answer confidently and wrongly, how to choose a model for a task and its data, and what you must tell users when a product uses AI.
description: A beginner course for developers who use ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude or DeepSeek every day and now have to build with them. Every lesson starts from a situation on the CodeDev learning platform - a hint bot that invented a parameter of an API that changed last year, a monthly bill ten times the estimate, an answer that changes every time a learner asks again, a support prompt that pasted a learner's email into a third-party API - and explains it with numbers you can check: tokens and context windows, temperature and repeatability, cost and latency per request, hallucination versus missing context, knowledge cutoff, choosing between a large and a small model or one that runs locally, data privacy and transparency duties under Vietnam's AI Law. No real model is called in the challenges: they run on recorded fixtures. 10 lessons with True/False quizzes on real prompts and logs, and TypeScript challenges graded by hidden tests.

learningOutcomes.text: Explain how an LLM generates text from tokens and probabilities and what happens when the context window is full
Estimate the cost and latency of an LLM feature from input and output tokens and a price table
Tell a hallucination from missing context or a knowledge cutoff, and reduce it with grounding and an allowed "I'm not sure"
Choose a model by task, cost, latency, repeatability and data sensitivity, including models that run locally
Keep sensitive data out of prompts and tell users clearly when they are dealing with AI

testedVersions.LLM fixtures: recorded responses, no live model (prices and limits need checking before publishing)

knownIssues: Challenges use recorded fixtures instead of a live model; calling a real API and comparing two models is self-practice
Model prices and context sizes change monthly: lessons use example price tables, not current list prices

lessons.title: How an LLM writes text: tokens, probabilities & the next word
What fits in the context window, and what gets cut
Temperature & repeatability: why the same question gets different answers
How to estimate the cost of an LLM feature from tokens
Latency: time to first token, output length & p95
How to choose a model: ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek or one that runs locally
The confident wrong answer: hallucination, missing context & knowledge cutoff
Grounding answers in documents and allowing "I'm not sure"
What never goes into a prompt: personal data, secrets & logs
Telling users it's AI: transparency duties in Vietnam's AI Law & the EU AI Act
